units.translation: where Turnebus has τὰ σώφροσιν εὐ μαιομένοις ἰδεῖν [to see the things of the wise with good fortune]. Hermann better: τὰ σώφρον᾽ εὖ μαιομένοις ἔχειν [for those who seek well to have the things of the wise].
objects of hatred to the wise
a wise, just, good, pious man
Woman, you speak wisely, as befits a wise man.
corruptly: to see the things of the wise with good fortune
for to the wise there are goads
I would call the sixth man more wise
and grant me to be far more wise than my mother
to see the things of the wise with good fortune
for those who seek well to have the things of the wise
